reply_text:
Checking Kimi quota via its `/usages` endpoint now.Kimi has quota to spare and its seats have a `view_image` tool. I'll check that Playwright can actually screenshot the site before briefing a seat.Yes, Kimi has quota. From `GET /coding/v1/usages`:

- **5-hour window:** 9 of 100 requests used.
- **Month:** 46% used; it resets on 23 October.

**The setup works too:**
- Kimi seats get a `view_image` tool (`kimi_api.clj:87-90`, checked live on 09-23). Z.AI seats don't.
- Playwright's Chromium is installed. The `npx playwright` in `~/code/excitement-to-evidence` works. The `@latest` one doesn't, because it wants a newer browser version than the one installed.
- I took a phone-sized (390×844) screenshot of the homepage and looked at it.

**The screenshot already shows something the text-only runs couldn't.** On a phone, the Minard chart sits just under the headline, but its annotations ("30 Aug facade found", "13 Sep codex-26 builds unrequested bookkeeping") are too small to read. So on mobile, the demo is a colourful stream of bands with no visible meaning. The readable text starts below it.

**My proposal is one Kimi run with images, focused on the demos.** Use the strategist persona again as the calibration reader, give it Playwright plus `view_image`, and have it take screenshots at laptop and phone widths. It would answer the question the Zai runs couldn't: do the images persuade? It would render pages the way a browser does, so the commented-out list wouldn't appear. It would go through `kimi-task.sh`, as your requisition rule requires, which commits one small excursion file to futon2.

It'll cost a handful of the 91 requests left in this window. Want me to send it?
